code.description: The error code for the failed request (not returned if request is successful)

message.description: Detailed information about the failed request (not returned if request is successful)

finish_reason.description: The reason why the task stopped. The value is stop when the task completes normally

message.description: The message returned by the model

content.description: The message content containing the generated image information

image.description: The URL of the generated image in PNG format. The link is valid for 24 hours

text.description: A textual element returned in place of an image. An element carrying only this field produced NO asset, so a caller keys completion off `image` rather than off the presence of a content element

role.description: The role of the message. Fixed as assistant

usage.description: The resource usage of this call. Only returned on success

input_image_count.description: The number of input images in the request. Returns 0 for text-to-image

input_image_type.description: The input image billing tier, qima_input_1k or qima_input_2k, determined by the output resolution pixel area

output_height.description: The height of the final output image in pixels

output_image_count.description: The actual number of output images returned

output_image_type.description: The output image billing tier, qima_output_1k or qima_output_2k, determined by the output resolution pixel area

output_width.description: The width of the final output image in pixels

info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "qwen/qwen-image-3.0", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. `x-comfy-router-input-modalities` records the media kinds the model is documented to accept; the request schema is shared across sibling models and may admit media kinds this model ignores. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.
info.title: qwen/qwen-image-3.0

schema.description: Request body for a Qwen multimodal image generation or edit. The `example` below is the COMFY ROUTER form and deliberately omits `model`, which Router fills from the `{model}` path segment; a direct v1 call to POST /proxy/qwen/api/v1/services/aigc/multimodal-generation/generation must add `model` to it. One example cannot serve both surfaces - this component is the Router input schema for BOTH qwen spellings, so an example naming either one is refused by the other model's route for naming a different model, while the omitting form is valid on both.

content.text: A single red maple leaf on a plain white background.

input.description: The input parameter object containing the request messages

messages.description: The request content array. Only single-round conversations are supported, so the array must contain exactly one object

content.description: The message content array. Text-to-image contains one text object; image editing contains 1-3 image objects and one text object

image.description: The URL or Base64 encoded data of an input image. 1-3 images are supported for image editing

text.description: The positive prompt that describes the image content, style, and composition to generate or edit

role.description: The role of the message sender. Must be set to user

model.description: The ID of the model to call for multimodal image generation and editing. Available values are qwen-image-3.0-pro and qwen-image-3.0. It is NOT in this schema's `required` list because Comfy Router fills it from the `{model}` path segment of /v2/models/qwen/{model}, so a Router caller omits it; a direct v1 call to the /proxy/ route must supply it.

parameters.description: Additional parameters to control image generation

n.description: The number of output images. Range 1-6, default is 1

negative_prompt.description: The negative prompt that describes content you do not want to appear in the image

prompt_extend.description: Whether to enable intelligent prompt rewriting. Default is true

prompt_extend_mode.description: The prompt rewriting method, direct (default, supported for T2I and I2I) or agent (T2I only)

seed.description: Random number seed to control randomness. Range [0, 2147483647]

size.description: The output image resolution in the format width*height, for example 1024*1024. The API accepts a pixel area between 262144 (512*512) and 6553600 (2560*2560) with an aspect ratio between 1:8 and 8:1. If not specified, the model automatically recommends a resolution based on the prompt

watermark.description: Whether to add a watermark. Default is false

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Qwen Image 3.0 models: the DashScope multimodal-generation response, forwarded unchanged. The operation is DIRECT-RETURN (`routerresult/classification.go` records `{provider: qwen, endpoint: /api/v1/services/aigc/multimodal-generation/generation}` as `ReturnModeDirect`), so the body a caller receives is this finished document from the one call rather than a task handle. `multimodalGenerationProxy`'s `ModifyResponse` meters it synchronously through `TrackUsage`, `QWEN_TASK_TYPE` registers no task checker, and the rewrite DELETES `X-DashScope-Async` — there is nothing to poll.
The generated image is at `output.choices[].message.content[].image`. DashScope documents that URL as valid for 24 HOURS, so download it promptly rather than storing it. Both `choices` and `content` are ARRAYS — `parameters.n` admits up to six images — so a caller reads every element rather than only the first, and that LEAF rather than the `output` container is what says a generation finished: a `content` element carrying only `text` produced no asset.
`usage` is DashScope's own accounting — `output_image_count` plus the `qima_input_*` / `qima_output_*` billing tiers it derives from the resolved resolution — and NOT the Comfy charge. Router reads those same fields to meter the call, but what a caller is charged is Comfy's rate card. DashScope documents `usage` as returned only on success.
`code` and `message` are DashScope's failure pair, absent on a success. Neither they nor `output` are constrained here, and `output` is deliberately NOT required: this operation's `Classification` names no `DirectState` reader, so Router treats a 2xx status as the whole success test and never inspects the body (`routerresult/extract.go`). A caller must key completion off the image leaf above rather than off the `200` alone.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.
